text:
maya: Heads up — after today's FP8 rollout to the H100 pool we're seeing a small-but-reproducible p99 spike on the customer 7B chat workload. p50 okay, p99 up ~75ms.

sam: which pool / config? dedicated or hosted?

maya: hosted H100-L40S mix, model pinned to fp8-optimized-variant, transformer-engine config set to 'fast-kernel-sched' per rollout doc. affected route: /v1/chat/generate for seq_len=1024 typical.

jordana: any change to batching heuristics? e.g. microbatching turned on?

maya: yes — we enabled adaptive microbatching with batch resonance heuristic (auto-burst=on). suspect interaction w/ KV cache eviction.

kai: can you paste the perf-bot profile snapshot? perf-bot: profile uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/2750001111/heatmap.png (attached)

maya: quick tl;dr from the heatmap: kernel fingerprint shows intermittent switch to int8-slowpath for matmul at 3.2% of tokens, correlates with p99 spikes. looks like kernel-selector misclassifying some layers.

ethan: ah that matches a case I saw last week — kernel selector falls back when sequence chunks split across microbatches and new KV indices cause unaligned strides. leads to nvrtc fallback path.

sam: do we have a minimal repro? small script to reproduce latency curve?

maya: yes repro script here:
```bash
# repro: simulates customer seq distribution + microbursts
python tests/repro_fp8_microburst.py --model gpt-7b-fp8 --seq 1024 --burst 8 --iterations 500
```

jordana: paste top of perf log around the spike (kernel names + occupancy)

maya: logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:41Z] kernel_selector: choose_kernel(matmul_fused_fp8, sm90_fast) -> SUCCESS
[2026-03-15T14:02:42Z] kernel_selector: choose_kernel(matmul_fused_fp8, sm90_fast) -> FALLBACK -> matmul_int8_slow
[2026-03-15T14:02:42Z] runtime: kv_cache_eviction: triggered_by=cache_pressure, evict_count=12
[2026-03-15T14:02:42Z] telemetry: batch_id=1724 latency_ms=312 p99
```

kai: eviction + fallback combo is suspicious. if eviction happens mid-request we might be losing reconstructed KV alignment and triggering different kernel paths.

ethan: can we force the selector to prefer fp8-path even when stride mismatch within tolerance? maybe add small tolerance mask for leading dim alignment.

sam: cautious — forcing might hide correctness bugs. need to validate quality (logprobs / sampling) before pushing.

jordana: agree. can we A/B route a small percentage to a selector tweak with extra checks + assert outputs equal within epsilon?

maya: set up canary at 1% on a subset of hosts. doing that now.

perf-bot: canary deployed: canary_id=c-2750001111-1 route=/v1/chat/generate traffic=1% hosts=5

kai: also worth measuring occupancy and SM utilization when fallback happens. I suspect the fallback kernel uses smaller tile sizes -> lower SM occupancy and more wave launches -> p99 hit.

maya: I ran nvprof windowed traces — occupancy drops from 78% to 34% during fallback windows. memory bandwidth stays high, but warp efficiency drops. attaching numbers: matmul_fast: 5.2 TFLOP/s, matmul_slow: 1.1 TFLOP/s.

ethan: big delta. suggests kernel-selector has a brittle stride heuristic. what triggers it? misaligned leading dim, or quantization calibration metadata mismatch?

maya: we also noticed that FP8 calibration metadata for layer norm scale was slightly different between rollout and baseline (maybe quant params updated). when rollout started some layers got new scale table which changed packing and led to different leading dims post-quant.

sam: so root cause might be calibration-induced layout change + microburst batching causing KvCache eviction and misaligned strides. multi-factor.

jordana: plan: 1) pause auto-burst for canary hosts, 2) add a selector tolerance path that prefers fp8 when fallback is only due to stride mismatch, 3) run numeric equivalence checks between fp8 preferred and fallback kernels, 4) metricize p50/p99 and sample outputs for QA.

maya: implementing 1 & 2 now. selector tweak diff:
```diff
- if (!aligned(leading_dim)) fallback_to_int8();
+ if (!aligned(leading_dim) && !only_stride_mismatch()) fallback_to_int8();
+ // only_stride_mismatch checks for packing-only mismatches and allows fp8 fast path
```

kai: make sure to gate with a feature flag: `fp8_selector_relax_stride` and a telemetry tag.

maya: added flag and telemetry. applying to canary hosts.

perf-bot: canary update: flag=fp8_selector_relax_stride=true on hosts [h-12, h-23, h-34, h-45, h-56]

sam: how long until we have stats?

maya: 20 minutes to get stable p99 numbers. I'll post graphs.

[20m later]

maya: quick update — the canary with relaxed selector: p99 down from +75ms to +12ms vs baseline. no apparent output divergence in sampled requests (KL divergence < 1e-6 on logprobs for 500 sampled prompts).

jordana: nice. what's the cost delta? any extra regressions?

maya: flops/throughput slightly higher (fast path used more often), CPU overhead to selector negligible. NV memory pressure slightly lower because we avoided re-launching smaller kernels.

ethan: next: we should add deterministic check in transformer-engine compile that preserves original leading-dim packing across quantization to avoid layout shifts. that prevents future calibration drift causing stride changes.

sam: file RFC for that change (impact on compiler + quant metadata) and assign owners. also add internal test that runs microburst workload through selector combinator for each new quant calibration.

maya: RFC created: ./docs/rfc/2026-03-15-fp8-packing-stability.md owner=@maya reviewers=@ethan,@jordana

perf-bot: telemetry snapshot: canary_p99_delta_ms=-63, canary_kl_divergence=9.4e-7, fastpath_pct=96.8%

kai: sounds like solid mitigation. schedule a staged rollout once RFC approved. also add a detector that alerts if selector flips >1% within 5m window.

sam: thanks team. great troubleshooting thread — saved a regression before a wide rollout. :tada:

maya: logging action items in the thread: pause auto-burst globally for 2 hours, merge selector tweak behind FF, RFC for packing stability, add microburst regression test, add selector flip alert.

ethan: i'll pick up the transformer-engine change after RFC review.

maya: closing loop in 48h with post-rollout metrics.

perf-bot: thread closed (archive after 30d)
